summary: Throwing a lit oil potion onto a hard floor reaches explode.c:explode_oil through dothrow.c:throwit -> breakobj. explode_oil extinguishes the potion, marks it LOST_EXPLODING, then splatter_burning_oil rolls the explosion damage and calls the fiery explosion path. The current JavaScript refusal skips both functions and incorrectly labels explode_oil as belonging to potion.c; the first C-owned RNG call is d(4,4) in explode.c:splatter_burning_oil.

source.branch: When a lit POT_OIL potion breaks, dothrow.c:breakobj calls explode_oil. For the investigated throw, dothrow.c:throwit reaches breakobj after the potion lands on a hard floor and passes breaktest. explode_oil saves obj->odiluted, extinguishes the lit source with end_burn, sets obj->how_lost to LOST_EXPLODING, and calls splatter_burning_oil; that function rolls 4d4 for undiluted oil or 3d4 for diluted oil and passes the damage to a fiery BURNING_OIL explosion.
callers: dothrow.c:throwit (1779-1791) calls breakobj after a thrown object lands on a hard tile and passes breaktest; dothrow.c:breakobj (2493-2502) calls explode_oil when the broken potion is lit POT_OIL.
potion.c:potionhit (1683-1688, 1866-1868) calls explode_oil when a lit oil potion hits the hero or a monster.
dependencies: rnd.c:d (175 onward): its return from d(diluted_oil ? 3 : 4, 4) initializes dmg in splatter_burning_oil and is consumed by the subsequent explode call; the recording reaches the undiluted d(4,4) branch.
timeout.c:end_burn (1804 onward): explode_oil calls end_burn(obj, TRUE) to extinguish the light before setting LOST_EXPLODING; its return is void.
explode.c:explode (199 onward): consumes the damage, location, BURNING_OIL source, and fiery type to apply the explosion; its return is void.
impossible(): called only when explode_oil receives an unlit object, to report the violated precondition; that branch is not reached by this recording.

evidence: The supplied diagnostic .cache/synthetic-scans/v15/wizard-throws-lit-oil-potion-to-floor.json reports the first difference at segment 0, step 31, key l: C has B at screen cell (0,33), while JavaScript has a space. At that point C logs d(4,4)=13 from splatter_burning_oil(explode.c:964), while the JavaScript log has rn2(100)=55 and the diagnostic lists the skipped path as unported potion.c explode_oil.

The C recording challenges/cases/v15/wizard-throws-lit-oil-potion-to-floor.session.json has the same step-31 call sequence, including obj_resists followed by d(4,4)=13 @ splatter_burning_oil(explode.c:964), and captures the lit-oil fiery explosion frames. The recording and queue entry are retained as the evidence for the observed behavior; neither is an implementation rule.

At nethack-c/upstream/src/dothrow.c:1780-1791, throwit calls breakobj after a thrown object lands on a hard tile and passes breaktest. At dothrow.c:2493-2502, breakobj marks potions in use and calls explode_oil only for POT_OIL with lamplit set. This is the active source route in the recording.

At nethack-c/upstream/src/explode.c:962-969, splatter_burning_oil rolls d(diluted_oil ? 3 : 4, 4) and passes the resulting damage to explode with type 11, BURNING_OIL, and EXPL_FIERY. At explode.c:971-983, explode_oil preserves odiluted, checks the lit invariant, calls end_burn(obj, TRUE), sets how_lost to LOST_EXPLODING, and invokes splatter_burning_oil. These are adjacent whole functions and the minimal source-port scope for this omitted behavior.

The same explode_oil function has another direct caller: potion.c:potionhit, at 1683-1688 when oil hits the hero and 1866-1868 when it hits a monster. Thus the function-family scope covers both throwing a lit potion and potion-impact entry points. The JavaScript stub labels the missing owner as potion.c, but the pinned C definitions for both functions are in explode.c.
